claims.claim: King of the Franks from 768 (crowned 9 October 768 at Noyon); King of the Lombards from 774; crowned Emperor by Pope Leo III on 25 December 800 at Old St. Peter's Basilica, Rome.

Birth date: current scholarship favors 2 April 748 (Matthias Becher's reading of the Annales Petaviani against the Easter-year); an older tradition gives 742 (Einhard's '72 at death', the Annals' 'about 71'); the walked FamilySearch record carries 0742. The record's value stands unaltered in the corpus; the scholarly range is recorded here.
Died 28 January 814 at Aachen; buried at the Palatine Chapel, Aachen (now Aachen Cathedral).

Parents: Pepin the Short and Bertrada of Laon; named after his grandfather Charles Martel. (The public walked corpus stages no parents for him — the walk's terminus — so the page honestly shows none recorded there.)
Louis the Pious (778–840, his son by Hildegard) survived him and succeeded as emperor; co-emperor from 11 September 813, sole rule from 28 January 814.

Louis the Pious's daughter Gisela, by his second wife Judith of Bavaria, married Eberhard of Friuli — this is the corpus's 'Gisela Markgräfin von Friaul 0820–0874', and therefore Charlemagne's granddaughter, not his daughter. Charlemagne's own daughter named Gisela was Hildegard's eighth child, born 781 in Italy.
